NoteNlpAccessor::align_sentences¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteNlpAccessor::align_sentences(const Note& other) const

Sentence-Level Alignment Of Two Notes¶

align_sentences(other) compares each cell of self against the matching cell of other one sentence at a time and returns the full alignment as a TokenBatch of tag-prefixed tokens. It is the sentence-granularity member of the diff / align family; see also align_tokens (word granularity), diff_words, diff_lines, and diff_chars.

How the comparison works¶

For each cell pair the two texts are first cut into sentences (the same sentence segmentation used elsewhere in Note — a run ending at ., !, or ? followed by whitespace, with common abbreviations kept whole). The two sentence lists are then aligned by their longest common subsequence: the longest ordered set of sentences that appear, unchanged, in both. Every sentence is emitted exactly once, in reading order, carrying a one-byte tag:

Tag

Meaning

Present in self

Present in other

=

unchanged — part of the common subsequence

yes

yes

-

removed — in self, not matched in other

yes

no

+

added — in other, not matched in self

no

yes

The tag is the first character of each emitted token; the sentence text follows with no separator. Recover the text with remove_prefix or a one-character substring, and filter by reading token[0].

Because align_* keeps the = tokens, the token stream for a cell is a complete transcript: replay it in order and you reproduce other from self. For a change-only view — the - and + tokens with the = sentences dropped — there is no separate diff_sentences spelling; call align_sentences and skip the tokens whose first byte is =.

The TokenBatch result¶

All tags from all cells are concatenated into the rank-1 Note batch.tokens(). The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1; cell r owns tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]). A cell whose two sides are identical contributes a run of = tokens (one per sentence), never an empty range — that empty-range case is what diff_words and the other diff_* methods produce.

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

The comparison is per cell and pairwise. self and other must have the same numel, or one of them may be a scalar (numel() == 1) that is broadcast against every cell of the other; any other shape is ignored beyond its cell count. Two rejections, both raising pluss::Error:

  • self in bytes mode → NoteNlpAccessor::align_sentences requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes).

  • unequal numel with neither side a scalar → NoteNlpAccessor::align_sentences expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

The alignment is O(m · n) in sentences per cell and fully deterministic: on a tie the walk emits the - (removal) before the + (insertion).

Example 1: A Substituted Sentence¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"One. Two. Three."})
                       .nlp().align_sentences(pluss::make_note({"One. Two changed. Three."}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["=One.", "-Two.", "+Two changed.", "=Three."]
offsets: [0, 4]

"One." and "Three." are shared, so they carry =. The middle sentence is a substitution: the old form leaves as -Two. and the new form arrives as +Two changed..

Example 2: Identical Cells Are All =¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"Stay put. Do not move."})
                       .nlp().align_sentences(pluss::make_note({"Stay put. Do not move."}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["=Stay put.", "=Do not move."]

Every sentence matched — two = tokens, no - or +.

Example 3: An Appended Sentence¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"First one. Second one."})
                       .nlp().align_sentences(pluss::make_note({"First one. Second one. Third one."}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["=First one.", "=Second one.", "+Third one."]

The two original sentences are unchanged; the extra sentence in other is the single + token.
